# IBM Planning Analytics budget model with an offline rule evaluator

> PaciolisCube: a driver-based IBM Planning Analytics (TM1) budget for a fictional
> Australian mining services group, published in the TM1 Git source format, with a
> Rust engine that parses and evaluates its rules without a TM1 server. Continuous
> integration recomputes the model on every push and fails if a figure moves.

The engine is the `pacioliscube` command line, built from source with Cargo; 0.3.0 on
PyPI was the last Python release. Entities, commercial rates and volumes are fictional. This repository was
named PaciolisCube until September 2026; the old URL redirects.

## Start

- [README](https://github.com/ryanduguid/planning-analytics-model#readme): what is in the repository, install and use.
- Install: clone the repository, then `cargo install --locked --path .`.
- Check the model's structure: `pacioliscube validate model`.
- Print a profit and loss from the shipped data: `pacioliscube report model --data examples --year FY2026-27 --version Budget`.

## Contents

- [model/](https://github.com/ryanduguid/planning-analytics-model/tree/main/model): the `tm1project.json` manifest, 13 dimensions, 5 cubes, 4 rule files and 8 TurboIntegrator processes.
- [src/](https://github.com/ryanduguid/planning-analytics-model/tree/main/src): rule parser, structural validator, cell store with weighted consolidation, CSV loader and command line.
- [examples/](https://github.com/ryanduguid/planning-analytics-model/tree/main/examples): fictional entities, rates and volumes, plus dated statutory rates and thresholds.
- [Model assumptions](https://github.com/ryanduguid/planning-analytics-model/blob/main/docs/model-assumptions.md): the source of every statutory figure and how it was confirmed.
